about: What to expect when in the U.S./Canada service year: recurring rules expanded by assets/js/view-calendar.js plus dated events (an explicit event replaces the rule occurrence it names in "rule"). Shape documented in view-calendar.js.

sources.service_manual: The A.A. Service Manual combined with Twelve Concepts for World Service, 2026-2028 edition (BM-31); printed page numbers
sources.final_reports: General Service Conference Final Reports 2017-2026; printed page numbers
sources.neta65: https://neta65.org/ events and NETA Area Handbook (rev. Nov 2024)
sources.research: Calendar audit C1/C2/C3 with verification passes, 2026-10-20 (corrections applied)

trustee_rotation.note: Regional trustees serve four one-year terms; each region elects every four years (Service Manual p.54). Trustees-at-large: U.S. and Canada staggered (four-year terms).

2018.place: Crowne Plaza Times Square, New York

2019.place: Crowne Plaza Times Square, New York

2022.place: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge

2023.place: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge

2024.place: New York Marriott at the Brooklyn Bridge

2027.source: 2025 Final Report p.45, p.85; aa.org event page

2028.source: 2025 Final Report p.45, p.85; aa.org board calendar

rules.title: Panel {P} delegates take office; Panel {P-2} has rotated off
rules.why: Delegates elected at the fall assemblies (and usually the area officers elected with them) start their two-year term. Panel P serves Jan 1 of P+1950 to Dec 31 of P+1951, so the outgoing panel served until Dec 31. GSR and DCM terms often line up with the panel.
rules.what_to_do: Until today the incoming delegate is a delegate-elect; GSO does not publish an incoming panel before rotation. New GSRs: this is a good moment to start with the Service Manual. In many areas new GSRs and DCMs (and alternate DCMs) also start two-year terms with the panel (pp. 8, 16). If not done yet: the group sends the district, area, intergroup/central office and GSO the new GSR's information (p. 12); read A.A.'s Legacy of Service (Appendix A) and the manual (p. 9); find a service sponsor (pp. 10, 17). A new DCM's first task is usually the first district meeting (p. 17).
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.110 (“All those elected usually take office January 1”); p.8 (GSR/DCM terms); 2024 Final Report p.71 (delegates serve until Dec 31; incoming panel not published before rotation); pp. 9, 10, 12, 16, 17 (new GSRs and DCMs)

rules.title: Election assemblies: half the areas elect Panel {P+1} delegates
rules.why: About half the areas elect each fall by Third Legacy Procedure. In even years the odd-panel areas (including Area 65) elect; in odd years the even-panel areas. This creates the rotating panels and keeps continuity at the Conference.
rules.what_to_do: Results go to GSO by Dec 1 and feed the December committee draw. Watch area websites for delegate-elects.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.20 (“usually scheduled in the fall”), p.110, p.121, p.124-125, Appendix M p.130 (Area 65 elects odd panels)

rules.title: Area election results due at GSO
rules.why: The sample election-assembly format asks the area secretary to send the names of the delegate, officers, committee members and GSRs present to the Conference secretary at GSO by December 1 (a suggested date: the formats are examples).
rules.what_to_do: After this date GSO knows the new panel and the committee draw can follow.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 Appendix D, election assembly step 14, p.110

rules.title: Delegates-elect (Panel {P+1}) get Conference dashboard access; outgoing delegates brief them
rules.why: On election each delegate goes on GSO's Conference mailing list and gets a dashboard password. Late in year two, outgoing delegates pass along a basic knowledge of Conference proceedings and send GSO the new area officers' contact details.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.32, p.33, p.34

rules.title: Conference committees drawn by lot for Panel {P+1}
rules.why: The Conference coordinator and the chair of the trustees’ Committee on the General Service Conference assign the first-year delegates by lot to the seats of the outgoing panel, with custom software and prioritized criteria. A delegate keeps the committee for both years; some also get Archives or IC/RF.
rules.what_to_do: Compare the real draw with the Predict page. Delegates usually hear in December or January.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.45 (“typically held in December of each year”), p.48; 2024 Final Report p.71

rules.title: Résumés due: {RT} candidates
rules.why: Regional trustee and trustee-at-large candidates must have their résumés at GSO (electronic or postmarked) by January 1 before the April Conference that elects them. Late résumés are returned; an area whose nominee withdraws after the deadline may not submit another.
rules.what_to_do: Areas pick candidates at their fall assemblies; the delegate sends the name to the trustees’ Nominating Committee.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.54 (election-year table), p.55

rules.title: Trustee nominees chosen at the Conference: {RT}
rules.why: Nominating sessions during Conference week (recently on the Wednesday afternoon) pick one nominee per opening by Third Legacy Procedure. For a regional trustee the voters are the region’s delegates plus an equal number drawn half from the Conference Committee on Trustees and half from the trustees’ Nominating Committee. The trustee and officer slates are presented for disapproval, if any.
rules.what_to_do: The region’s delegates vote, so ask your delegate about the candidates beforehand.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.50, p.55-58; 2023 Final Report p.65 (random selection of extra voters); Wednesday elections: 2019 Final Report p.4, 2022 Final Report p.5, 2025 Final Report p.4

rules.title: Trustee-at-large regional caucuses (regional lunch)

rule.when: Conference week, before the trustee-at-large nominating session (trustee-at-large election years only)

rules.why: Before the trustee-at-large nominating session, each region's delegates caucus, generally at a regional lunch, and cut the list to one name per U.S. region or two per Canadian region (at most 6 U.S. or 4 Canada candidates). Canada elects in 2027 and 2031, the U.S. in 2029 and 2033 (staggered seats). In U.S. years the Southwest delegates, Area 65's included, choose the region's one name. The manual gives no day.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.57

rules.title: Next year’s trustee openings announced ({RT+1})
rules.why: GSO tells delegates and area officers in the regions due to elect at the next Conference (a May mailing), posts the notice on aa.org (June 11, 2025; June 2, 2026) and runs it in Box 4-5-9. The Class A (nonalcoholic) trustee notice comes out about the same time (May 22, 2025; June 1, 2026).
rules.what_to_do: If your region elects next year, areas choose candidates at their fall assemblies.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.54; aa.org news and announcements (June 11, 2025; June 2, 2026)

rules.title: Class A (nonalcoholic) trustee résumés due (when a seat opens)
rules.why: When a Class A seat opens at the next Conference, résumés are due August 31 (2024, 2025 and 2026). Finalists are interviewed at the winter board weekend and elected at the annual meeting after the Conference. The date applies only when aa.org announces a Class A opening (notices May 22, 2025 and June 1, 2026). Expected Aug 31, 2027 for Kerry M.'s seat at the 78th GSC (not yet announced). Listed only in years before a seat is due to rotate (2028, 2030, 2031 and 2032 Conferences); no seat rotates after the 79th GSC, so 2028 applies only if a vacancy arises or Tim M. does not serve a second term.
rules.what_to_do: Members may suggest professionals who are friends of A.A. Check aa.org that a Class A seat is open this cycle.
rules.source: Procedure No. 4 (aa.org Class A submission reminder, Aug 2025); aa.org notices May 22, 2025 and June 1, 2026; 2026 Final Report p.107

rules.title: GSO staff desk rotation (expected)
rules.why: Most GSO staff change assignments about every two years, so the staff secretary of a Conference committee may change. Recent rotations: Aug 23, 2022 and September 2025 (when a Self-Support/Finance desk was added). The cadence is not strict.
rules.what_to_do: Check the Staff page after the next Final Report.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.C-71; 2023 Final Report p.94; 2026 Final Report p.66

rules.title: General Service Board weekend (1st quarterly)
rules.why: Trustees’ committees meet and the board holds a General Sharing Session. The year’s AAWS and Grapevine budgets come to this first meeting after January 1; Class A finalists are interviewed; the board approves the workload plan, and the final Conference agenda follows.
rules.what_to_do: Watch for the final agenda and then the background material.
rules.source: GSB bylaws, Service Manual 2026-2028 p.140 (“fifth Monday following the close of a calendar quarter”); p.151, p.160 (budgets); p.61 (General Sharing Session); 2024 Final Report p.70

rules.title: Board annual meeting: new trustees elected; closing breakfast
rules.why: The 2nd quarterly board meeting is the Saturday right after the Conference closes. It adjourns for the annual meeting of members, which elects the trustees (including those chosen in Conference week) and receives the annual report; the board then elects its officers. AAWS and Grapevine elect their directors at their own annual meetings, and rotating trustees say farewell at the closing breakfast.
rules.what_to_do: Trustee and director rosters change on this date, not in the summer.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.40 (closing breakfast), p.137, p.139-140, p.144, p.153

rules.title: General Service Board weekend (3rd quarterly)
rules.why: The board approves the chair’s appointments to trustees’ committees, so new trustees and appointed committee members start here; trustees’ committees review mid-year reforecasts and begin work on the Conference’s Advisory Actions.
rules.what_to_do: A proposal status grid follows within about 3 weeks; the Quarterly Report 2-4 months later.
rules.source: GSB bylaws, Service Manual 2026-2028 p.140; 2021 Final Report p.49; 2026 Final Report p.97, p.108

rules.title: General Service Board weekend (4th quarterly)
rules.why: Trustees’ committees decide which proposed agenda items go to the next Conference. From October 2026 the incoming Conference’s committee chairs attend this weekend instead of the January one (the Service Manual still says January).
rules.what_to_do: Watch for the preliminary Conference agenda in November.
rules.source: GSB bylaws, Service Manual 2026-2028 p.140; 2026 Final Report p.49, p.72, p.85; 2024 Final Report p.70

rules.title: AAWS and Grapevine board meetings (week before each quarterly GSB meeting)
rules.why: The AAWS and Grapevine bylaws put a regular board meeting in the week before each quarterly GSB meeting (AAWS often meets the Thursday before). AAWS meets up to eight times a year; Grapevine quarterly plus four planning meetings.
rules.what_to_do: Literature prices and publishing news usually follow; see AAWS Highlights and the Quarterly Report.

rules.title: AAWS and Grapevine regular board meetings (week before the post-Conference board meeting)
rules.why: Both corporate bylaws require a regular board meeting in the week before every quarterly GSB meeting, including the 2nd quarterly meeting held the Saturday after the Conference.
rules.what_to_do: Check aa.org's board calendar for the actual day. Each board may postpone, defer or omit a regular meeting by majority agreement (pp. 147, 155), so this may not happen every year.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.140, p.147, p.155

rules.title: Proposed agenda item deadline for the {GSC+1} Conference
rules.why: Proposals received by September 30, 11:59 pm go to the next April’s Conference; later ones roll over to the Conference after that. (Under the workload pilot it was Sept 15; a 2024 Advisory Action moved it to no earlier than Sept 30, and the trustees chose Sept 30.)
rules.what_to_do: In Area 65 a proposal has to clear the September Fall Assembly first, so start with your group and district in the summer.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.38 (Advisory Action); 2025 Final Report p.85; aa.org proposed agenda item page (“on or before September 30, 2026, 11:59 pm”)

rules.title: October feedback calls on proposed agenda items
rules.why: After the Sept 30 cutoff, trustees’ committee chairs hear their Conference committees on the proposals before the trustees decide at the fall board weekend; the trustees’ GSC Committee chair meets Agenda, Policy/Admissions and Report and Charter. It replaced the pre-January committee call in the Service Manual (p.49).
rules.what_to_do: First-year delegates take part once their committee is drawn.
rules.source: 2025 Final Report p.85; 2023 Final Report p.66; 2026 Final Report p.41; Service Manual 2026-2028 p.49, p.63

rules.title: Preliminary agenda for the {GSC+1} Conference
rules.why: The list of proposals forwarded, ongoing and standing items, released “as of November” after the fall board weekend.
rules.what_to_do: Ask your delegate or area for it: it is the first look at next April’s topics.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.70 (Conference communications plan); 75th GSC preliminary agenda (“as of November 2024”)

rules.title: Proposal status grid sent to Conference members
rules.why: Under a 2025 Advisory Action GSO sends Conference members a grid of every proposal and its status after each board weekend: Aug 20, 2025, Nov 22, 2025 and Feb 6, 2026.
rules.what_to_do: Delegates often share it at area committee meetings.
rules.source: 2026 Final Report p.84

rules.title: Final agenda for the {GSC} Conference
rules.why: The final list of agenda items, with the committee workload distribution, comes out “as of February” after the winter board weekend.
rules.what_to_do: Area 65 districts start preparing for the March mock committees.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.70; 76th GSC final agenda list (“as of February 2026”)

rules.title: Background material for the {GSC} Conference reaches members
rules.why: Background on every agenda item goes out in English, French and Spanish at the same time: Feb 17-21, 2023; Feb 16-23, 2024; Feb 20-24, 2025; Feb 17-20, 2026 (even for the early Apr 14, 2024 Conference). A list of proposals not forwarded follows 1-2 weeks later.
rules.what_to_do: GSRs and districts study it before the Spring Assembly mock committees.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.45; 2022 Final Report p.78 (simultaneous release); 2024 Final Report p.70; 2025 Final Report p.85; 2026 Final Report p.83

rules.title: Pre-Conference sessions on the {GSC} agenda

rule.label: between background material and the Conference

rules.why: Areas, districts and groups study the Conference agenda and tell the delegate their group conscience before the Conference.
rules.what_to_do: Read the background on your delegate's committee and bring your group's conscience to the district or area session.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.22, p.33; background timing: 2026 Final Report p.83

rules.title: Conference Manual and pre-Conference video meetings
rules.why: The Conference Manual reaches members; joint trustees’/Conference committee meetings and other sessions now meet by video before Conference week (2024 Manual Mar 14-23).
rules.what_to_do: A sign of how much Conference work happens before the delegate travels.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.38, p.70; 2026 Final Report p.42

rules.title: Policy/Admissions pre-Conference video meeting
rules.why: About 1-2 weeks before the Conference, Policy/Admissions meets by video to admit observers and seat temporary replacements (an alternate when a delegate cannot attend): Apr 9, 2024 and Apr 13, 2025.
rules.what_to_do: If your delegate cannot go, this is where the alternate is seated.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.38 (Advisory Action); 2023 Final Report Advisory Actions

rules.title: The {GSC} General Service Conference
rules.why: The Conference meets for one week, usually in April, in New York. Committees meet jointly with their trustees’ committees early in the week, then deliberate; the last days are floor discussion and votes (Advisory Actions need two-thirds). A delegates-only meeting is often held before opening day.
rules.what_to_do: Follow your delegate’s reports; the area’s sense from the spring mock committees goes with them.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.40, p.45, p.63, p.92, p.97, p.104; 2025 Final Report p.45, p.85; 2026 Final Report p.48

rules.title: Committees elect {Y+1} chairs from first-year members (Panel {P})
rules.why: Each committee elects next year’s chair and alternate chair by plurality at its last meeting, always from its first-year members (260 of 260 since 2017); primary committees first, then Archives and IC/RF. Next year’s Delegate Chair is drawn from the hat at the delegates-only dinner among first-year delegates not elected chair or alternate.
rules.what_to_do: A first-year delegate has about a 1 in 4 or 5 chance of chairing their committee next year.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.45; 2024 Final Report p.46; 2025 Final Report p.4; 2026 Final Report p.4

rules.title: Conference committee chairs’ orientation
rules.why: An orientation for the newly elected committee chairs shortly after the Conference (May 28, 2025); the trustees’ committee asked for it to be early.
rules.what_to_do: For first-year delegates just elected chair or alternate.
rules.source: 2026 Final Report p.83; 2024 Final Report p.71; 2025 Final Report p.9

rules.title: {GSC} Conference Final Report posted
rules.why: The complete record of the Conference with rosters of delegates, committees, trustees and staff. The 76th GSC report was posted Sept 4, 2026; print codes show July-October in 2017-2026. A 2026 Advisory Action had AAWS offer the 2026 report in print for purchase; if sales do not cover production costs, there will be no print version for the 2027 Conference.
rules.what_to_do: This app’s main source: load the new year when it appears.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.43 (“summer”); aa.org news (Sept 4, 2026); report print codes 2017-2026; 2026 Final Report p.38

rules.title: Delegates' Conference report-backs

rule.label: the weeks and months after the Conference

rules.why: Reporting back to groups, districts and the area is a vital part of every delegate's job. Delegates report at assemblies and district meetings, visit groups where they can, and may offer reports to intergroup/central offices. Areas are asked to cover the delegate's report-back travel.
rules.what_to_do: Ask your DCM when the delegate reports in your district, and ask for a printed or digital copy to pass on to your group.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.36 (expenses), p.37 (Reporting Back)

rules.title: Box 4-5-9 {label} issue
rules.why: GSO’s quarterly news bulletin, online only since 2024, posted later than its season name (Winter Mar 6, 2026; Spring Jun 24, 2026; Summer Aug 18, 2026; Fall Dec 11, 2025). The summer issue carries the Conference summary; trustee openings and forum news appear here.
rules.what_to_do: The standard source for GSR reports.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.11, p.76, p.91; aa.org news and announcements (posting dates 2025-2026)

rules.title: Annual Anonymity Letter to the Media
rules.why: The Public Information desk sends the annual anonymity letter to more than 30,000 media outlets (January in 2021-2023, February in 2024-2026).
rules.what_to_do: Local PI committees often re-use it.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.72; 2021 Final Report p.54; 2024 Final Report p.107; 2026 Final Report p.115

rules.title: New edition of The A.A. Service Manual
rules.why: Updated every two years with Conference actions (the 2026-2028 edition is marked “Revised: September 2026”; the 2024-2026 edition was in print Dec 20, 2024).
rules.what_to_do: Page numbers in this app follow the 2026-2028 printing; the next edition will shift them.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.II, p.71; aa.org news (Dec 20, 2024; Feb 13, 2025)

rules.title: World Service Meeting
rules.why: Delegates from general service structures worldwide meet every two years, alternating New York and another country; the two trustees-at-large represent U.S./Canada. It shares experience and sets no policy.
rules.what_to_do: Its final report is posted on aa.org around the following February.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.57, p.62, p.72, p.124; 2025 Final Report p.28-29

rules.title: REDELA (Meeting of the Americas)
rules.why: The zonal meeting of the Americas in the years without a WSM, usually late September or early October; the trustees-at-large attend.
rules.what_to_do: Reported by the trustees-at-large in the next Final Report.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.57, p.62; 2021 Final Report p.101; 2026 Final Report p.31-32

rules.title: A.A. International Convention
rules.why: Every five years, on a June or July weekend; about 50,000 expected (Vancouver 2025: 33,731). Registration opens about 10 months ahead.
rules.what_to_do: Plan travel early; hotel blocks fill fast.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.39, p.72; 2026 Final Report p.95-96

rules.title: Regional Forums: Western Canada, Eastern Canada, Pacific, Southeast
rules.why: Each region has a Forum every two years. Even years: Western Canada, Eastern Canada, Pacific and Southeast (every even year since 2016). Forums are free weekends of sharing with trustees, directors and GSO/Grapevine staff.
rules.what_to_do: Any member may attend any region’s Forum; dates appear on aa.org about a year ahead.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.62, p.73, p.93; 2026 Final Report p.98

rules.title: Regional Forums: Northeast, East Central, West Central, Southwest
rules.why: Odd years: Northeast, East Central, West Central and Southwest (every odd year since 2017).
rules.what_to_do: The Southwest Forum is Area 65’s own; dates appear on aa.org about a year ahead.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.62, p.73, p.93; 2026 Final Report p.98

rules.title: Southwest Regional Forum
rules.why: The board’s visit to the Southwest region in odd years: San Antonio 2017, Houston 2019, virtual 2021, El Paso 2023, Albuquerque 2025, Kansas City 2027. Free; the Southwest regional trustee moderates.
rules.what_to_do: The best chance to meet trustees and GSO staff without going to New York.
rules.source: 2026 Final Report p.98; 2025 Final Report p.102; earlier Final Reports (IC/RF reports)

rules.title: Southwest Regional Delegates Assembly (SWRDA), Oklahoma City
rules.why: An annual meeting of past delegates, past regional trustees, the Southwest trustee and the serving delegates and alternates, run by the region (hosted by Area 57). It works as a mock Conference to prepare the delegates (Mar 13-15, 2026; Mar 12-14, 2027).
rules.what_to_do: The new delegate’s first regional gathering, about a month before their first Conference.
rules.source: 2021 Final Report p.89 (“Every March, Area 57 hosts …”); NETA Area Handbook p.12-13; Area 68 service calendar (2026-2027 dates)

rules.title: Southwest Regional A.A. Service Assembly (SWRAASA)
rules.why: The region’s own service weekend in even years, the second weekend of October (Friday-Sunday around the second Saturday), rotating among the 11 Southwest areas (Tulsa Oct 7-9, 2022; Richardson 2024, Area 65; Baytown 2026, Area 67; 2028 Area 66). The Southwest alternate delegates carry its business.
rules.what_to_do: Workshops open to all members; delegates and the trustee usually present.
rules.source: 2017 Final Report p.74; 2021 Final Report p.89; 2025 Final Report p.158; nwta66.org SWRAASA page

rules.title: Founders’ Day, Akron
rules.why: A.A.’s anniversary weekend in Akron, the weekend closest to June 10 (Dr. Bob’s last drink, 1935), hosted by Akron Intergroup (June 6-8, 2025; June 12-14, 2026).
rules.what_to_do: Many groups and areas mark it locally.
rules.source: 2023 Final Report p.130 (“On the closest weekend to June 10th …”); 2017 Final Report p.76

rules.title: Anniversary of the 1955 St. Louis Resolution
rules.why: On July 3, 1955, at the Twentieth Anniversary Convention in St. Louis, A.A. adopted the Resolution that made the General Service Conference guardian of the Traditions and sole successor to the co-founders (Appendix L).
rules.what_to_do: A good day to reread Appendices K and L (the Conference Charter and the Resolution).
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 pp. 128-129

rules.title: Gratitude Month
rules.why: The general manager sends an annual Gratitude Month message in November; many areas and districts hold gratitude dinners, and year-end Seventh Tradition giving peaks.
rules.what_to_do: A natural time for group Seventh Tradition and Birthday Plan discussions.
rules.source: 2024 Final Report p.16; 2018 Final Report p.70; 2023 Final Report p.130

rules.title: National A.A. Archives Workshop
rules.why: An annual Fellowship workshop (not run by GSO) that the GSO archivist attends; late September or mid-September (Sep 29-Oct 3, 2021 San Antonio; Sep 26-29, 2024 Des Moines; Sep 10-13, 2026 Tacoma).
rules.what_to_do: For area archives committees and Archives delegates.
rules.source: 2017 Final Report p.29; 2019 Final Report p.25; host-area event listings 2024 and 2026

rules.title: National Corrections Conference
rules.why: A Fellowship-run corrections service conference held each fall since 2017, usually in November, attended by GSO and Grapevine/La Viña staff.
rules.what_to_do: For corrections committees.
rules.source: 2017 Final Report p.28, p.46; 2018 Final Report p.65; 2026 Final Report p.21

rules.title: Intergroup/Central Office seminar
rules.why: An annual seminar of intergroup and central office managers, attended by AAWS and Grapevine board members and staff (Nov 2016, Oct 2017, Sept/Oct 2018; San Antonio, Nov 6-8, 2026). The Service Manual calls it the Intergroup/Central Office/AAWS (ICOAA) Seminar: the first, in 1986, discussed literature distribution, pricing and discounts and ways to work together, and seminars are now held each year (p. 167).
rules.what_to_do: Matters for the Dallas and Fort Worth intergroups.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.167; 2017 Final Report p.29, p.52; 2018 Final Report p.37

rules.title: NETA 65 GSR/DCM orientations (three Sundays)
rules.why: Three identical orientations each January (central, west and east sites) on the whole structure from the group to the Conference, right after the new panel takes office.
rules.what_to_do: The best on-ramp for a new GSR or anyone learning the structure.
rules.source: NETA Area Handbook (rev. Nov 2024) p.15-16; 2019 Final Report p.62; 2025 Final Report p.157

rules.title: NETA 65 Winter Area Committee Meeting
rules.why: One of four area committee meetings a year (Feb 12, 2023; Feb 18, 2024; Feb 16, 2025; Feb 22, 2026). DCMs, officers and committee chairs vote.
rules.what_to_do: The new panel’s first area business meeting, before the pre-Conference Spring Assembly.
rules.source: neta65.org past events (2023-2026); 2019 Final Report p.62; NETA Area Handbook (rev. Nov 2024)

rules.title: Delegate’s Corner pre-Conference sessions (agenda review, mock-committee training)
rules.why: Online sessions before the Spring Assembly: a review of the final agenda items and training for mock-committee chairs and scribes (Feb 24, Mar 7 and Mar 10 in 2026). Expect them earlier when the Conference is early.
rules.what_to_do: Where members learn the year’s agenda items before the area takes its sense on them.
rules.source: NETA UpWord Fall 2026 p.21; NETA Area Handbook (rev. Nov 2024) p.13

rules.title: NETA 65 Spring Assembly: pre-Conference mock committees
rules.why: Members split into mock committees on the final agenda items and report back, giving the delegate the area’s conscience (“informed, not instructed”). Mar 17-19, 2023; Mar 14-16, 2025; Mar 20-22, 2026.
rules.what_to_do: The main chance for a GSR to bring the group’s input to the delegate. Register early for a mock-committee seat.
rules.source: 2019 Final Report p.62; 2021 Final Report p.92; 2025 Final Report p.157; neta65.org past events

rules.title: NETA 65 Spring Area Committee Meeting

rule.label: a Sunday 1–3 weeks before the Conference

rules.why: Quarterly area business on a Sunday one to three weeks before the Conference (Apr 7, 2024, GSC Apr 14; Apr 6, 2025, GSC Apr 27; Apr 12, 2026, GSC Apr 26). The 77th Conference opens Apr 11, 2027, so expect it by early April.
rules.what_to_do: The last area business meeting near the Conference.
rules.source: neta65.org past events (2024-2026); 2025 Final Report p.45 (2027 Conference dates)

rules.title: NETA 65 Summer Assembly: delegate’s Conference report-back
rules.why: The delegate reports on the Conference just held (Jun 23-25, 2023; Jun 14-16, 2024; Jun 27-29, 2025; Jun 26-28, 2026). Districts hold their own report-backs through the summer.
rules.what_to_do: Hear what the Conference decided and carry it back to your group.
rules.source: Service Manual 2026-2028 p.5, p.37 (report-backs); 2019 Final Report p.62; neta65.org past events

rules.title: NETA 65 Summer Area Committee Meeting
rules.why: Quarterly business (Jul 16, 2023; Jul 14, 2024; Jul 13, 2025; Jul 19, 2026). Draft proposed agenda items for the Fall Assembly appear around now.
rules.what_to_do: Watch for the proposals the area will vote on in September.
rules.source: neta65.org past events; NETA Area Handbook (rev. Nov 2024) p.15

rules.title: NETA 65 Fall Assembly (area votes on proposed agenda items)
